The club was formed on 25 January 1890, making it Spain's second oldest sporting club solely devoted to football, after [[Recreativo de Huelva]].{{cite web |date=9 October 2012 |title=The day Spanish football was born |url=http://www.marca.com/2012/09/10/en/football/spanish_football/1347305537.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206222215/http://www.marca.com/2012/09/10/en/football/spanish_football/1347305537.html |archive-date=6 February 2015 |access-date=6 February 2015 |publisher=Marca}}{{cite web |date=11 October 2012 |title=How Glasgow man Hugh McColl helped set up Spain's oldest football club |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/news/how-glasgow-man-hugh-mccoll-helped-set-up-spains-oldest-football-club-104007n.19098806 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217011754/http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/news/how-glasgow-man-hugh-mccoll-helped-set-up-spains-oldest-football-club-104007n.19098806 |archive-date=17 February 2015 |access-date=6 February 2015 |work=Evening Times}}{{Cite web |title=Scottish Influence on Spanish Football |url=https://www.scottishfootballmuseum.org.uk/news/scottish-influence-on-spanish-football/ |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=Scottish Football Museum |language=en}} The Scottish-born [[Edward F. Johnston|Edward Farquharson Johnston]] was one of Sevilla's founders, also becoming their first president. On 14 October 1905, the club's articles of association were registered in the Civil Government of Seville under the presidency of the Jerez-born José Luis Gallegos Arnosa. Sevilla are also the most successful football club in [[Andalusia]] in terms of titles, with eighteen Andalusian Cups,{{cite web|title=Honours|url=https://sevillafc.es/en/the-club/honours|access-date=2022-01-03|website=sevillafc.es|archive-date=6 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106153022/https://sevillafc.es/en/the-club/honours|url-status=live}} one [[La Liga]] title in [[1945–46 La Liga|1945–46]], five [[Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup]] titles ([[1935 Copa del Presidente de la República|1935]], [[1939 Copa del Generalísimo|1939]], [[1947–48 Copa del Generalísimo|1948]], [[2006–07 Copa del Rey|2007]] and [[2009–10 Copa del Rey|2010]]), one [[Supercopa de España|Spanish Super Cup]] ([[2007 Supercopa de España|2007]]), a [[List of UEFA club competition winners|record]] seven [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cups / UEFA Europa Leagues]] ([[2005–06 UEFA Cup|2006]], [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|2007]], [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|2014]], [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League|2015]], [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|2016]], [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|2020]], and [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League|2023]]) and one [[UEFA Super Cup]] ([[2006 UEFA Super Cup|2006]]). They were also designated by the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics]] as the [[IFFHS World's Best Club|World's Best Club]] in 2006 and 2007, thus being the first club to achieve this distinction in two consecutive years. The reserve team [[Sevilla Atlético]], founded in 1958, currently play in {{Spanish football updater|Sevilla Atlético}}. Other clubs related to Sevilla FC include their women's team. The rowing team that defends its crest in the yearly Sevilla-Betis [[Boat racing|boat race]] is not a section of the club but a call-up of registered-as-supporters professional rowers from the various rowing clubs of Seville. The club's home ground is the 43,883-seat [[Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium]]. It is located in the neighborhood of [[Nervión, Seville]], and is named after [[Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán]], who was the president of Sevilla for 17 years. Sevilla has a long-standing rivalry with cross-city rival [[Real Betis]], and matches between the pair are the [[Seville derby]]."}}
